summary: Claude Code can run a session in an isolated Git worktree, a second working directory of the same repository. It creates each one under .claude/worktrees/<name> at the repository root. Nothing in this repository's .gitignore covered that directory, so git status in the main checkout listed .claude/worktrees/ as untracked whenever a session ran in a worktree.

This pull request adds one line, .claude/worktrees/, to .gitignore. The main checkout then stays clean while sessions work in worktrees. The rest of .claude/, such as the tracked .claude/settings.json, is unaffected, and no code, test, or packaging step reads this file.

groups.title: The ignore entry
groups.kicker: One .gitignore line for Claude Code's worktree directory
intro: A .gitignore pattern that holds a slash before its end is anchored to the directory that holds the .gitignore. So .claude/worktrees/ matches only that directory at the repository root, and only directories, because of the trailing slash.

checks.text: In a temporary repository that uses this head's .gitignore, git check-ignore -v matches .claude/worktrees/example at line 13, and matches none of .claude/settings.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, or a nested sub/.claude/worktrees/.

The pull request body's Testing steps run mkdir -p .claude/worktrees/example and then rmdir on the example. That leaves an empty, ignored .claude/worktrees/ behind even when it did not exist before, which the body's last sentence does not say. The review lists this as a suggestion.
